stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether a smiling expression makes cartoons seem funnier. They recruited 90 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a pen between their teeth, which produces a smile. Participants in the other condition held a pen between their lips, which prevents a smile. The researchers then recorded the rating from 1 to 10 that each participant gave to a set of cartoons.

Researchers collected data from 350 adults. For each one, they recorded the number of stressful life events in the past year and the number of colds in the past year. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.33.

Researchers investigated whether keeping a gratitude journal raises well-being. They recruited 110 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition wrote down three things they were grateful for every night for a month. Participants in the other condition wrote down three things they had done every night for a month. The researchers then recorded each participant's rating of life satisfaction on a scale from 1 to 10 at the end of the month.

Researchers investigated whether caffeine improves attention. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition drank coffee containing 200 milligrams of caffeine. Participants in the other condition drank decaffeinated coffee that tasted the same. The researchers then recorded the number of targets that each participant correctly detected in a ten-minute computer task. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

rows.group: The group that drank caffeinated coffee
The group that drank decaffeinated coffee

stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 1,000 students. For each one, they recorded intelligence test score at age 11 and average school grade at age 16. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.60.

Researchers investigated whether a phone conversation reduces what drivers notice. They recruited 64 licensed drivers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a hands-free phone conversation while using a driving simulator. Participants in the other condition used the driving simulator without a phone. The researchers then recorded the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice.

Researchers investigated whether nausea after a new taste produces an aversion to that taste. They recruited 40 laboratory rats and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Rats in one condition drank sweetened water and were then given an injection that causes mild nausea. Rats in the other condition drank sweetened water and were then given a harmless salt-water injection. The researchers then recorded the volume in milliliters of sweetened water that each rat drank the next day.

Researchers investigated whether an expected reward reduces children's later interest in drawing. They recruited 60 preschool children who enjoyed drawing and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were promised a certificate for drawing and received it. Children in the other condition drew with no reward mentioned. The researchers then recorded the number of minutes that each child chose to spend drawing during free time one week later.

Researchers collected data from 400 high school students. For each one, they recorded the average number of hours slept per night and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.45.

Researchers investigated whether a new drug reduces anxiety. They recruited 150 adults diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition took the new drug every day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition took a placebo pill that looked identical every day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard anxiety questionnaire after eight weeks.

Researchers investigated whether spreading study sessions out improves long-term retention. They recruited 90 high school students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition studied a list of 40 words in six ten-minute sessions on six different days. Participants in the other condition studied the same list in a single sixty-minute session. The researchers then recorded the number of words out of 40 that each participant recalled on a test one month later.

Researchers investigated whether mindfulness meditation lowers stress. They recruited 84 office workers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition practiced mindfulness meditation for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition listened to an audiobook for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded the level of the stress hormone cortisol in a saliva sample from each participant.
Researchers collected data from 450 adults. For each one, they recorded optimism score and the number of days of illness in a year. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.30.

Researchers investigated whether the color of a drink affects the ability to identify its flavor. They recruited 70 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition tasted ten fruit drinks whose colors did not match their flavors. Participants in the other condition tasted the same ten drinks with matching colors. The researchers then recorded the number of flavors out of ten that each participant named correctly.

Researchers investigated whether praise increases hand raising in class. They recruited 50 second-grade students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were praised by the teacher each time they raised a hand before speaking. Children in the other condition received no special response when they raised a hand. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child raised a hand during one week.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether guided hints help children learn to solve puzzles. They hypothesized that help from an adult would affect problem-solving skill.

**Participants.** The sample was 64 five-year-old children, recruited from one city. Parents gave informed consent, each child gave assent, and the plan was approved by an institutional review board. Families could withdraw at any time.

**Method.** The children were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Children in one condition solved practice puzzles with hints from an adult that were gradually reduced. Children in the other condition solved the same practice puzzles alone. The researchers recorded the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help.

**Results.** The group that received hints: mean new puzzles solved (out of 10) = 7.2. The group that practiced alone: mean new puzzles solved (out of 10) = 4.6. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Why do people sometimes fail to help in an emergency?**

**Source A.** In an experiment, 80 students were randomly assigned to be alone or with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants who were alone reported the smoke after a mean of 58 seconds; those in groups took a mean of 196 seconds (p = 0.01), and many never reported it.

**Source B.** In interviews after a staged emergency, participants who had not helped often said that they 'assumed someone else had already called for help' or that 'nobody else looked worried, so it could not be serious.'

**Source C.** Researchers observed 300 staged incidents in which a person dropped a bag of shopping in the street. Help was offered in 82 percent of incidents on quiet streets and in 41 percent of incidents on crowded streets.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the participants to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: In Pavlov's experiments, dogs salivated to food, and later to a tone that had been paired with food. The food was which of the following?

options.why: Correct. The unconditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning.
The conditioned response is in classical conditioning, the learned response to a previously neutral stimulus.
The unconditioned response is in classical conditioning, the natural, unlearned response to a stimulus.
The conditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the originally neutral stimulus that triggers a response after being paired with another stimulus.

questions.explanation: The unconditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning.

questions.stem: After an argument with his roommate, Luis meditates and listens to music to settle his feelings. Which kind of coping is this?

options.why: Correct. Emotion-focused coping is the reducing of stress by managing one's emotional reaction rather than the stressor.
Immune suppression is the weakening of the body's defenses against illness during long-term stress.
Hypertension is persistently high blood pressure, which is made more likely by chronic stress.
Problem-focused coping is the reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it.

questions.explanation: Emotion-focused coping is the reducing of stress by managing one's emotional reaction rather than the stressor.

questions.stem: A therapist and client rank situations from 'looking at a picture of a spider' to 'holding a spider.' What is this ranked list called?

options.why: A token economy is the behavioral system in which people earn tokens for desired behavior and exchange them for rewards.
Aversion therapy is the behavioral treatment that pairs an unwanted behavior with an unpleasant stimulus.
Applied behavior analysis is the use of the principles of conditioning to increase helpful behaviors and reduce harmful ones.
Correct. A fear hierarchy is a list of feared situations arranged from the least to the most frightening.

questions.explanation: A fear hierarchy is a list of feared situations arranged from the least to the most frightening.

questions.stem: Lena is told that she scored as well as or better than 90 percent of the students who took a test. Which statistic is this?

options.why: The median is the middle score when the scores are placed in order.
A negative skew is a distribution with a few extremely low scores, which pull the mean below the median.
Correct. A percentile rank is the percentage of scores in a distribution that fall at or below a given score.
The mode is the score that occurs most often.

questions.explanation: A percentile rank is the percentage of scores in a distribution that fall at or below a given score.

questions.stem: A researcher flips a coin to decide whether each volunteer goes into the treatment group or the control group. Which procedure is this?

options.why: Correct. Random assignment is the placing of participants in experimental conditions by chance.
Generalizability is the extent to which the findings of a study apply to people beyond the sample.
Sampling bias is a flaw in selecting participants that makes the sample unlike the population.
A representative sample is a sample whose characteristics match those of the population it is drawn from.

questions.explanation: Random assignment is the placing of participants in experimental conditions by chance.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes sensorineural deafness?

options.text: The theory that we hear pitch because the rate of nerve impulses matches the frequency of the sound
options.why: That describes frequency theory.

options.text: The theory that groups of neurons take turns firing so that together they match high sound frequencies
options.why: That describes volley theory.

options.text: The ability to tell where a sound comes from, using differences in timing and loudness between the two ears
options.why: That describes sound localization.

options.text: Hearing loss caused by damage to the hair cells of the cochlea or to the auditory nerve
options.why: Correct. This is what sensorineural deafness means.

questions.explanation: Sensorineural deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the hair cells of the cochlea or to the auditory nerve.

questions.stem: After Mia talks back, her mother gives her extra chores, and she talks back less often. Being given the chores is an example of which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Positive punishment is the weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it.
Negative punishment is the weakening of a behavior by removing a pleasant stimulus after it.
Negative reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus after it.
Positive reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by adding a pleasant stimulus after it.

questions.explanation: Positive punishment is the weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the directionality problem in this study?

options.text: It is unclear how many people took part
options.why: The sample size is stated.

options.text: It is unclear whether the correlation is positive or negative
options.why: The sign of r shows the direction of the relationship.

options.text: It is unclear whether the two measures were recorded
options.why: Both measures were recorded.

options.text: It is unclear whether the first measure influences the second or the second influences the first
options.why: Correct. A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

questions.explanation: A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the personality disorder marked by lasting distrust and suspicion of others?

options.why: Correct. Paranoid personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by lasting distrust and suspicion of others.
Avoidant personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by extreme sensitivity to rejection and avoidance of social contact.
Dependent personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an excessive need to be taken care of and by clinging, submissive behavior.
Narcissistic personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an exaggerated sense of self-importance and a need for admiration.

questions.explanation: Paranoid personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by lasting distrust and suspicion of others.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes size constancy?

options.text: The perception that an object keeps the same color under different lighting
options.why: That describes color constancy.

options.text: The perception that an object keeps the same size even when its image on the retina changes
options.why: Correct. This is what size constancy means.

options.text: The perception of motion when a series of still images or lights is shown in quick succession
options.why: That describes apparent movement.

options.text: The perception that an object keeps the same shape even when the viewing angle changes
options.why: That describes shape constancy.

questions.explanation: Size constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same size even when its image on the retina changes.

questions.stem: A child realizes that water poured from a short glass into a tall one could be poured back to give the same level as before. Which concept does this show?

options.why: Object permanence is the understanding that things continue to exist when they are out of sight.
Correct. Reversibility is the understanding that an action can be undone to return things to their original state.
Theory of mind is the understanding that other people have their own thoughts, beliefs and feelings.
Egocentrism is the difficulty that young children have in taking another person's point of view.

questions.explanation: Reversibility is the understanding that an action can be undone to return things to their original state.

questions.stem: To open a combination lock, Wes tries 000, then 001, then 002, and so on until it opens. Which problem-solving strategy is he using?

options.why: Correct. An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure that guarantees a solution.
Functional fixedness is the inability to see that an object can be used for something other than its usual purpose.
Convergent thinking is thinking that narrows the possibilities down to the single best answer.
A mental set is the tendency to approach a problem in a way that has worked before, even when it no longer works.

questions.explanation: An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure that guarantees a solution.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes cognitive appraisal?

options.text: The theory that positive emotions widen a person's awareness and help build lasting skills and resources
options.why: That describes the broaden-and-build theory.

options.text: The interpretation of a situation, which shapes the emotion a person feels
options.why: Correct. This is what cognitive appraisal means.

options.text: A cultural rule about which emotions may be shown, when and to whom
options.why: That describes a display rule.

options.text: The idea that the expression on a person's face can influence the emotion the person feels
options.why: That describes the facial-feedback hypothesis.

questions.explanation: Cognitive appraisal is the interpretation of a situation, which shapes the emotion a person feels.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes Cluster B?

options.text: The group of personality disorders marked by anxious or fearful behavior: avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive
options.why: That describes Cluster C.

options.text: A lasting, rigid pattern of behavior and inner experience that differs from cultural expectations and impairs functioning
options.why: That describes a personality disorder.

options.text: The group of personality disorders marked by odd or eccentric behavior: paranoid, schizoid and schizotypal
options.why: That describes Cluster A.

options.text: The group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic
options.why: Correct. This is what Cluster B means.

questions.explanation: Cluster B is the group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic.

questions.stem: English speakers say 'white house' while Spanish speakers say 'casa blanca', with the adjective second. This difference is one of which of the following?

options.why: A morpheme is the smallest unit of language that carries meaning.
A phoneme is the smallest distinctive unit of sound in a language.
Correct. Syntax is the rules for ordering words into sentences.
Grammar is the whole system of rules in a language that lets people communicate.

questions.explanation: Syntax is the rules for ordering words into sentences.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a behavior that is repeated because it happened by chance just before a reward?

options.why: Correct. Superstitious behavior is a behavior that is repeated because it happened by chance just before a reward.
A secondary reinforcer is a reinforcer, such as money or praise, that gets its power through association with other rewards.
Instinctive drift is the tendency of a trained animal to return to its natural, inborn behaviors.
The law of effect is Thorndike's principle that behaviors followed by good outcomes become more likely and those followed by bad outcomes become less likely.

questions.explanation: Superstitious behavior is a behavior that is repeated because it happened by chance just before a reward.

questions.stem: Neither the participants nor the assistants who recorded the results knew which condition each participant was in. What is this procedure called?

options.why: Random sampling is how participants are chosen from a population.
Correct. Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.
In a single-blind procedure only the participants are unaware.
That is a therapy technique, not a research control.

questions.explanation: Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes somnambulism?

options.text: Sleepwalking, which occurs during deep NREM sleep
options.why: Correct. This is what somnambulism means.

options.text: A sleep disorder in which breathing repeatedly stops during sleep, causing brief awakenings
options.why: That describes sleep apnea.

options.text: A sleep disorder with ongoing difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep
options.why: That describes insomnia.

options.text: A sleep disorder with sudden, uncontrollable attacks of sleep, often straight into REM sleep
options.why: That describes narcolepsy.

questions.explanation: Somnambulism is sleepwalking, which occurs during deep NREM sleep.

questions.stem: Why is this study not an experiment?

options.why: Experiments also use numerical data.
Sample size does not determine the research method.
Experiments also test hypotheses.

options.text: The researchers did not manipulate a variable or randomly assign anyone to conditions
options.why: Correct. An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.explanation: An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.stem: After considering several careers and trying two internships, Nadia commits to becoming a nurse. Which identity status is this?

options.why: Identity diffusion is the identity status of a person who has neither explored options nor made a commitment.
Identity moratorium is the identity status of a person who is actively exploring options but has not yet made a commitment.
Identity foreclosure is the identity status of a person who has made a commitment without exploring options.
Correct. Identity achievement is the identity status of a person who has explored options and made a commitment.

questions.explanation: Identity achievement is the identity status of a person who has explored options and made a commitment.

questions.stem: Before taking part, each participant was told what the study would involve and what the risks were, and then agreed to take part. Which ethical guideline does this meet?

options.why: Correct. Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.
Confidentiality is keeping participants' data private.
That is a research procedure, not an ethical guideline.
Debriefing happens after the study.

questions.explanation: Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.

questions.stem: What is the independent variable in this study?

options.text: The number of animals in the study
options.why: This is the sample size, not a variable the researchers changed.
This was measured, not manipulated: it is the dependent variable.

options.text: The type of injection given after drinking
options.why: Correct. The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.
This is a procedure for forming the groups, not a variable.

questions.explanation: The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

questions.stem: A toddler who knows the word 'dog' sees a cow for the first time and calls it a dog. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: A prototype is the best or most typical example of a category.
Correct. Assimilation is the interpretation of a new experience in terms of an existing schema.
A schema is a mental framework that organizes and interprets information.
A concept is a mental grouping of similar objects, events, ideas or people.

questions.explanation: Assimilation is the interpretation of a new experience in terms of an existing schema.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes authoritarian parenting?

options.text: The parenting style that sets strict rules and expects obedience, with little warmth or discussion
options.why: Correct. This is what authoritarian parenting means.

options.text: A person's characteristic emotional reactivity and intensity, which appears early in life
options.why: That describes temperament.

options.text: The parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm
options.why: That describes authoritative parenting.

options.text: The parenting style that makes few demands and sets few limits
options.why: That describes permissive parenting.

questions.explanation: Authoritarian parenting is the parenting style that sets strict rules and expects obedience, with little warmth or discussion.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a graph in which each point shows one individual's values on two variables?

options.why: The correlation coefficient is the number from −1.00 to +1.00 that shows the direction and strength of a relationship.
A negative correlation is a relationship in which one variable rises as the other falls.
The third variable problem is the possibility that an unmeasured factor causes the relationship between two correlated variables.
Correct. A scatterplot is a graph in which each point shows one individual's values on two variables.

questions.explanation: A scatterplot is a graph in which each point shows one individual's values on two variables.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the tendency, when judging other people's behavior, to overestimate personal traits and underestimate the situation?

options.why: The self-serving bias is the tendency to credit our successes to ourselves and blame our failures on outside factors.
Relative deprivation is the feeling of being worse off than the people one compares oneself with.
An optimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as temporary, specific and caused by outside factors.
Correct. The fundamental attribution error is the tendency, when judging other people's behavior, to overestimate personal traits and underestimate the situation.

questions.explanation: The fundamental attribution error is the tendency, when judging other people's behavior, to overestimate personal traits and underestimate the situation.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a growth mindset?

options.text: A test that predicts a person's ability to learn or perform in the future
options.why: That describes an aptitude test.

options.text: The belief that intelligence can be developed through effort and learning
options.why: Correct. This is what a growth mindset means.

options.text: The belief that intelligence is set and cannot be changed
options.why: That describes a fixed mindset.

options.text: The boost in performance that comes from awareness that another group is negatively stereotyped
options.why: That describes stereotype lift.

questions.explanation: A growth mindset is the belief that intelligence can be developed through effort and learning.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes out-group homogeneity bias?

options.text: The tendency to see the members of other groups as all alike
options.why: Correct. This is what out-group homogeneity bias means.

options.text: The tendency to hold on to a belief even after the evidence for it has been discredited
options.why: That describes belief perseverance.

options.text: The discomfort a person feels when their actions and attitudes conflict, which motivates a change in one of them
options.why: That describes cognitive dissonance.

options.text: The tendency to search for and favor information that supports what one already believes
options.why: That describes confirmation bias.

questions.explanation: Out-group homogeneity bias is the tendency to see the members of other groups as all alike.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the Big Five trait of being calm and secure rather than anxious and moody?

options.why: Extraversion is the Big Five trait of being sociable, outgoing and energetic.
Openness to experience is the Big Five trait of being imaginative, curious and willing to try new things.
Correct. Emotional stability is the Big Five trait of being calm and secure rather than anxious and moody.
Agreeableness is the Big Five trait of being kind, trusting and cooperative.

questions.explanation: Emotional stability is the Big Five trait of being calm and secure rather than anxious and moody.

questions.stem: A diagram labels every nerve that lies outside the brain and spinal cord. Which part of the nervous system does the diagram show?

options.why: Correct. The peripheral nervous system is the sensory and motor nerves that connect the brain and spinal cord to the rest of the body.
The central nervous system is the brain and spinal cord.
The sympathetic nervous system is the division of the autonomic nervous system that arouses the body for fight or flight.
The parasympathetic nervous system is the division of the autonomic nervous system that calms the body and conserves energy.

questions.explanation: The peripheral nervous system is the sensory and motor nerves that connect the brain and spinal cord to the rest of the body.

questions.stem: A patient describes the death of his mother in a monotone voice with no expression on his face. Which symptom is this?

options.why: Correct. Flat affect is a lack of emotional expression in the face and voice.
A delusion is a false belief, often of persecution or grandeur, that a person holds despite clear evidence against it.
Catatonia is a disturbance of movement in which a person may remain motionless for hours or move without purpose.
A hallucination is a sensory experience, such as hearing voices, that occurs without any outside stimulus.

questions.explanation: Flat affect is a lack of emotional expression in the face and voice.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the desire to do something to gain a reward or avoid a punishment?

options.why: An approach-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which one option has both attractive and unattractive features.
An approach-approach conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two attractive options.
Correct. Extrinsic motivation is the desire to do something to gain a reward or avoid a punishment.
An avoidance-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two unattractive options.

questions.explanation: Extrinsic motivation is the desire to do something to gain a reward or avoid a punishment.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: The two groups differed in intrinsic motivation to draw at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

options.text: The children promised a certificate were given newer pens to draw with
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

options.text: One group differed from the other in an expected reward
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: Of two identical twins with the same genetic risk for schizophrenia, only the one who lived through severe trauma develops it. Which model best explains this?

options.why: Comorbidity is the presence of two or more disorders in the same person at the same time.
The biopsychosocial model is the view that disorders result from the interaction of biological, psychological and social factors.
Correct. The diathesis-stress model is the view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience.
An eclectic approach is the use of techniques from several types of therapy, depending on the client's problem.

questions.explanation: The diathesis-stress model is the view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience.

questions.stem: Two two-year-olds sit next to each other, each building with their own blocks and not speaking. Which kind of play is this?

options.why: The personal fable is the belief of adolescents that they are unique and that bad things will not happen to them.
Emerging adulthood is the period from about 18 to the mid-twenties, between adolescence and full independence.
The imaginary audience is the belief of adolescents that everyone is watching and judging them.
Correct. Parallel play is the play of young children who play side by side without interacting.

questions.explanation: Parallel play is the play of young children who play side by side without interacting.

questions.stem: A patient is shown a picture of a key in the left visual field. He cannot name it but can pick out a key with his left hand. Which condition does he most likely have?

options.why: Correct. A split brain is the condition in which the two hemispheres cannot communicate because the corpus callosum has been cut.
An fMRI is a scan that shows brain activity by tracking blood flow.
Lesioning is the destruction of a small area of brain tissue to study its function.
An EEG is a recording of the electrical waves that sweep across the brain's surface.

questions.explanation: A split brain is the condition in which the two hemispheres cannot communicate because the corpus callosum has been cut.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes epigenetics?

options.text: The influence of environmental factors, such as upbringing and experience, on behavior and mental processes
options.why: That describes nurture.

options.text: The approach that explains behavior through natural selection of traits that helped ancestors survive and reproduce
options.why: That describes the evolutionary perspective.

options.text: The study of how the environment changes whether genes are expressed without changing the DNA itself
options.why: Correct. This is what epigenetics means.

options.text: Research that compares identical and fraternal twins to estimate the influence of heredity
options.why: That describes a twin study.

questions.explanation: Epigenetics is the study of how the environment changes whether genes are expressed without changing the DNA itself.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the disorder in which a person has at least two weeks of depressed mood or loss of interest, with other symptoms such as changes in sleep and appetite?

options.why: Mania is a state of extreme energy, overconfidence, racing thoughts and little need for sleep.
Bipolar II disorder is the disorder in which a person alternates between depression and a milder form of mania called hypomania.
Bipolar I disorder is the disorder in which a person has full manic episodes, usually alternating with depression.
Correct. Major depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has at least two weeks of depressed mood or loss of interest, with other symptoms such as changes in sleep and appetite.

questions.explanation: Major depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has at least two weeks of depressed mood or loss of interest, with other symptoms such as changes in sleep and appetite.

questions.stem: After two neurons fire together repeatedly, the synapse between them becomes more efficient. What is this process called?

options.why: Correct. Long-term potentiation is the strengthening of the connections between neurons after repeated activation, which is the biological basis of memory.
The central executive is the part of working memory that directs attention and coordinates the other parts.
The visuospatial sketchpad is the part of working memory that briefly holds images and spatial information.
The phonological loop is the part of working memory that briefly holds spoken and written words.

questions.explanation: Long-term potentiation is the strengthening of the connections between neurons after repeated activation, which is the biological basis of memory.

questions.stem: Students are asked whether each word on a list rhymes with 'cat'. Which level of processing does this task use?

options.why: Automatic processing is the encoding of information, such as space, time and frequency, without conscious effort.
Correct. Phonemic encoding is the encoding of a word based on its sound.
Semantic encoding is the deep encoding of a word based on its meaning.
Explicit memory is the memory of facts and experiences that a person can consciously recall and state.

questions.explanation: Phonemic encoding is the encoding of a word based on its sound.

questions.stem: Can the researchers conclude that the average number of hours slept per night causes a change in grade point average?

options.text: No, because correlations can only be calculated in experiments
options.why: Correlations are calculated in non-experimental studies.

options.text: Yes, because the sample was large
options.why: A large sample does not turn a correlation into evidence of causation.

options.text: No, because a correlation does not show cause and effect
options.why: Correct. Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

options.text: Yes, because the correlation is not zero
options.why: Any nonzero correlation still leaves the cause unknown.

questions.explanation: Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

questions.stem: Kim remembers exactly where she sat and what she ate at her tenth birthday party. Which kind of memory is this?

options.why: Procedural memory is the implicit memory of how to perform skills and actions.
Prospective memory is the memory to carry out a planned action in the future.
Semantic memory is the explicit memory of facts and general knowledge.
Correct. Episodic memory is the explicit memory of personally experienced events.

questions.explanation: Episodic memory is the explicit memory of personally experienced events.

questions.stem: Because his neighbor looked after his cat last month, Abe feels he should help the neighbor move house. Which norm is guiding him?

options.why: Correct. The social reciprocity norm is the expectation that people will help those who have helped them.
Altruism is unselfish concern for the welfare of others.
Burnout is the physical and emotional exhaustion that results from long-term stress at work.
The social responsibility norm is the expectation that people will help those who need help, even at a cost to themselves.

questions.explanation: The social reciprocity norm is the expectation that people will help those who have helped them.

questions.stem: After months of use, Dan needs twice as much of a drug to feel the effect that one dose used to give him. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: A reuptake inhibitor is a drug that keeps a neurotransmitter in the synapse longer by blocking its reabsorption.
An agonist is a drug that increases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by mimicking it.
Correct. Tolerance is the need for larger doses of a drug to get the same effect after repeated use.
An antagonist is a drug that decreases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by blocking its receptors.

questions.explanation: Tolerance is the need for larger doses of a drug to get the same effect after repeated use.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the comparing of oneself with people who are doing worse?

options.why: A self-fulfilling prophecy is an expectation that leads a person to act in ways that make the expectation come true.
Correct. Downward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing worse.
An internal locus of control is the belief that a person controls their own outcomes through their own actions.
The mere exposure effect is the tendency to like something more simply because we have encountered it repeatedly.

questions.explanation: Downward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing worse.

questions.stem: Hearing that a man lost his job, Viv assumes he must have been a bad worker. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: An implicit attitude is an attitude that a person holds without being aware of it.
Discrimination is unjustified negative behavior toward a group and its members.
A stereotype is a generalized belief about a group of people.
Correct. The just-world phenomenon is the tendency to believe that people get what they deserve.

questions.explanation: The just-world phenomenon is the tendency to believe that people get what they deserve.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the serial position effect?

options.text: The finding that study spread over time produces better long-term memory than study crammed together
options.why: That describes the spacing effect.

options.text: The tendency to remember the first and last items in a list better than the middle ones
options.why: Correct. This is what the serial position effect means.

options.text: The tendency to remember the first items in a list well
options.why: That describes the primacy effect.

options.text: The tendency to remember the last items in a list well
options.why: That describes the recency effect.

questions.explanation: The serial position effect is the tendency to remember the first and last items in a list better than the middle ones.

questions.stem: After a stroke, Mr. Lee understands what people say but can only produce slow, broken speech. Which area was most likely damaged?

options.why: Correct. Broca's area is the area in the left frontal lobe that controls speech production.
Contralateral control is the arrangement in which each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body.
Wernicke's area is the area in the left temporal lobe that controls language comprehension.
Hemispheric specialization is the tendency for each side of the brain to handle certain functions, such as language in the left hemisphere.

questions.explanation: Broca's area is the area in the left frontal lobe that controls speech production.

questions.stem: A wave of electrical charge moves down an axon from the cell body to the terminals. What is this wave called?

options.why: The refractory period is the brief pause after a neuron fires during which it cannot fire again.
Correct. The action potential is the brief electrical charge that travels down the axon when a neuron fires.
Depolarization is the change in which positive ions rush into the axon and make the inside less negative.
The all-or-nothing principle is the rule that a neuron either fires at full strength or does not fire at all.

questions.explanation: The action potential is the brief electrical charge that travels down the axon when a neuron fires.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
That is an in-depth study of one individual.
Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.
That is explaining the study to participants afterward.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: Scores on the odd-numbered questions of a test closely match scores on the even-numbered questions. Which quality does the test have?

options.why: Test-retest reliability is the consistency of scores when the same people take the same test twice.
Predictive validity is the extent to which test scores forecast the future performance they are meant to predict.
Correct. Split-half reliability is the consistency of scores between two halves of the same test.
Standardization is the giving and scoring of a test in the same way for everyone, and the comparison of scores with a pretested group.

questions.explanation: Split-half reliability is the consistency of scores between two halves of the same test.

questions.stem: All of the subjects in this study were drawn from one group: 90 high school students. What does this most limit?

options.text: Whether a cause-and-effect conclusion can be drawn
options.why: Random assignment, not the sample, allows the causal conclusion.

options.text: Whether the study had a control group
options.why: The study had a comparison condition.

options.text: How far the findings can be generalized to other populations
options.why: Correct. A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

options.text: Whether the dependent variable was operationally defined
options.why: The measure was clearly defined.

questions.explanation: A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

questions.stem: An eight-month-old learns about a rattle by shaking it, looking at it and putting it in her mouth. Which of Piaget's stages is she in?

options.why: The preoperational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 2 to 7, in which children use words and images but cannot yet reason logically.
The formal operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 12 on, in which people can reason about abstract and hypothetical ideas.
Correct. The sensorimotor stage is Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions.
The concrete operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 7 to 11, in which children think logically about real objects and events.

questions.explanation: The sensorimotor stage is Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the cultural pattern that gives priority to the goals of the group and defines identity by group membership?

options.why: Multiculturalism is the view that the different cultural groups in a society should be valued and should keep their identities.
Correct. Collectivism is the cultural pattern that gives priority to the goals of the group and defines identity by group membership.
The false consensus effect is the tendency to overestimate how many other people share our opinions and behaviors.
A social trap is a situation in which people who each pursue their own interest end up harming everyone.

questions.explanation: Collectivism is the cultural pattern that gives priority to the goals of the group and defines identity by group membership.

questions.stem: Four studies of child development report these correlation coefficients: −0.70, +0.28, −0.86, −0.44. Which coefficient shows the strongest relationship?

options.why: −0.44 is closer to zero.
+0.28 is closer to zero.
−0.70 is closer to zero.
Correct. Strength is the distance from zero, whatever the sign; −0.86 is farthest from zero.

questions.explanation: The sign of a correlation shows its direction; its distance from zero shows its strength. −0.86 is farthest from zero.

questions.stem: Before her wedding, Rosa feels nervous and excited, and the feeling gives her energy to prepare. Which kind of stress is this?

options.why: Correct. Eustress is the positive, motivating stress that comes from a challenge.
Distress is the negative stress that harms well-being and performance.
A stressor is an event or situation that a person sees as threatening or challenging.
The fight-or-flight response is the response to stress in which the sympathetic nervous system prepares the body to attack or escape.

questions.explanation: Eustress is the positive, motivating stress that comes from a challenge.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes wisdom?

options.text: The category of character strengths that includes teamwork, fairness and leadership
options.why: That describes justice.

options.text: The category of character strengths that includes bravery, honesty and perseverance
options.why: That describes courage.

options.text: The category of character strengths that includes forgiveness, humility and self-control
options.why: That describes temperance.

options.text: The category of character strengths that includes creativity, curiosity and love of learning
options.why: Correct. This is what wisdom means.

questions.explanation: Wisdom is the category of character strengths that includes creativity, curiosity and love of learning.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the reduced sensitivity that follows constant, unchanging stimulation?

options.why: Sensory interaction is the way one sense influences another, as when smell affects taste.
Weber's law is the principle that two stimuli must differ by a constant proportion, not a constant amount, to be noticed.
Correct. Sensory adaptation is the reduced sensitivity that follows constant, unchanging stimulation.
Synesthesia is the condition in which stimulating one sense produces an experience in another sense.

questions.explanation: Sensory adaptation is the reduced sensitivity that follows constant, unchanging stimulation.

questions.stem: After the study, the researchers explained its full purpose to every participant and answered their questions. What is this called?

options.why: Correct. Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.
Replication is repeating a study.
A placebo is an inactive treatment.
Consent is obtained before the study.

questions.explanation: Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.

questions.stem: In a drug trial, some patients receive a sugar pill that looks exactly like the real medication. The sugar pill is which of the following?

options.why: Effect size is the measure of how large the difference or relationship found in a study is.
A confounding variable is a factor other than the independent variable that differs between groups and could explain the results.
Correct. A placebo is an inactive substance or treatment that looks like the real one.
The experimental group is the group in an experiment that receives the treatment being tested.

questions.explanation: A placebo is an inactive substance or treatment that looks like the real one.

questions.stem: After getting food poisoning from fish, Carl feels sick at the smell of fish for years. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Biological preparedness is the inborn readiness to learn some associations, such as taste and nausea, more easily than others.
One-trial conditioning is learning that happens after a single pairing of two stimuli.
Correct. A taste aversion is a learned dislike of a food that was followed by illness.
Counterconditioning is the replacing of an unwanted response to a stimulus with a new response, by pairing the stimulus with something pleasant.

questions.explanation: A taste aversion is a learned dislike of a food that was followed by illness.

questions.stem: Mila constantly seeks out unfamiliar music, foreign films and trips to places she has never been. Which form of sensation seeking is this?

options.why: Boredom susceptibility is the form of sensation seeking that involves a strong dislike of repetition and routine.
Disinhibition is the form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties.
Thrill and adventure seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities.
Correct. Experience seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles.

questions.explanation: Experience seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles.

questions.stem: Why is this study not an experiment?

options.why: Experiments also test hypotheses.

options.text: The researchers did not manipulate a variable or randomly assign anyone to conditions
options.why: Correct. An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.
Sample size does not determine the research method.
Experiments also use numerical data.

questions.explanation: An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.stem: A man has no memory of a frightening accident he was in as a child. In psychodynamic theory, which defense mechanism explains this?

options.why: Correct. Repression is the defense mechanism of pushing anxiety-arousing thoughts and memories out of awareness.
Reaction formation is the defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses.
Regression is the defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development.
Sublimation is the defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities.

questions.explanation: Repression is the defense mechanism of pushing anxiety-arousing thoughts and memories out of awareness.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes anterograde amnesia?

options.text: A progressive brain disease that destroys memory and then other mental abilities
options.why: That describes Alzheimer's disease.

options.text: The inability of adults to remember events from the first few years of life
options.why: That describes infantile amnesia.

options.text: The loss of memories from before an injury or illness
options.why: That describes retrograde amnesia.

options.text: The inability to form new memories after an injury or illness
options.why: Correct. This is what anterograde amnesia means.

questions.explanation: Anterograde amnesia is the inability to form new memories after an injury or illness.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep?

options.why: Correct. Restoration is the repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep.
The consolidation theory is the theory that dreaming helps sort and strengthen the day's memories.
The activation-synthesis theory is the theory that dreams are the brain's attempt to make sense of random neural activity during sleep.
Memory consolidation is the strengthening of memories that takes place during sleep.

questions.explanation: Restoration is the repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep.

questions.stem: After the study, the researchers explained its full purpose to every participant and answered their questions. What is this called?

options.why: Correct. Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.
Consent is obtained before the study.
Replication is repeating a study.
A placebo is an inactive treatment.

questions.explanation: Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.

questions.stem: After taking a drug, a person's reactions slow, speech slurs and judgment weakens. Which type of drug is this most likely to be?

options.why: A stimulant is a drug, such as caffeine or cocaine, that speeds up neural activity and body functions.
An opioid is a drug, such as heroin, that relieves pain by acting on endorphin receptors and is highly addictive.
Correct. A depressant is a drug, such as alcohol, that slows neural activity and body functions.
A hallucinogen is a drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input.

questions.explanation: A depressant is a drug, such as alcohol, that slows neural activity and body functions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the second phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body stays highly aroused to cope with a continuing stressor?

options.why: Correct. The resistance phase is the second phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body stays highly aroused to cope with a continuing stressor.
The general adaptation syndrome is Selye's three-phase description of the body's response to long-term stress: alarm, resistance and exhaustion.
The exhaustion phase is the third phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body's resources run out and illness becomes more likely.
The alarm reaction is the first phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the sympathetic nervous system is suddenly activated.

questions.explanation: The resistance phase is the second phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body stays highly aroused to cope with a continuing stressor.

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.why: Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.
This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.
A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.stem: A person sees the world entirely in shades of gray because only one type of cone, or none, works. Which condition is this?

options.why: The opponent-process theory is the theory that color is processed in opposing pairs: red–green, blue–yellow and black–white.
Dichromatism is a form of color vision deficiency in which one of the three types of cones does not work.
Correct. Monochromatism is a rare form of color blindness in which a person sees only shades of gray.
Prosopagnosia is the inability to recognize faces, even familiar ones, after brain damage.

questions.explanation: Monochromatism is a rare form of color blindness in which a person sees only shades of gray.

questions.stem: Not wanting to upset the team's harmony, the members of a committee keep their doubts to themselves and approve a risky plan. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Groupthink is the kind of thinking in which the desire for agreement in a group overrides a realistic evaluation of alternatives.
Group polarization is the strengthening of a group's existing opinions after the members discuss them.
Social facilitation is the improved performance on simple or well-learned tasks in the presence of others.
Diffusion of responsibility is the reduced sense of personal duty to act when other people are present.

questions.explanation: Groupthink is the kind of thinking in which the desire for agreement in a group overrides a realistic evaluation of alternatives.

questions.stem: Scores on a test are normally distributed with a mean of 70 and a standard deviation of 15. About what percentage of scores are between 55 and 85?

options.why: This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
Correct. About 68% of scores fall within one standard deviation of the mean.

questions.explanation: About 68% of scores fall within one standard deviation of the mean. (55 and 85 are one standard deviation from the mean; 40 and 100 are two.)

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of problem-solving skill

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of problem-solving skill.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Problem-solving skill was defined as the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The group that received hints solved more new puzzles. On average, the value was 7.2 for the group that received hints and 4.6 for the group that practiced alone, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent and assent: parents consented and each child agreed to take part. (Also acceptable: approval by an institutional review board; the right to withdraw.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 64 five-year-old children from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The group that received hints solved more new puzzles. (7.2 compared with 4.6).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that help from an adult affects problem-solving skill. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to help from an adult. The finding illustrates scaffolding within the zone of proximal development: temporary support lets a child master what they could not yet do alone.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Why do people sometimes fail to help in an emergency?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: People are less likely to help when others are present, because each person feels less responsible and looks to others to decide how to act.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, participants who were alone reported smoke after 58 seconds, but those in groups of five took 196 seconds.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through the bystander effect and diffusion of responsibility: when others are present, each person feels less personal responsibility to act.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, participants said that 'nobody else looked worried, so it could not be serious.'

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through informational social influence: in an unclear situation, people use the behavior of others as evidence of what is happening, so if nobody reacts, each person concludes there is no emergency.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
